title: I started my first game a few days ago and it’s already playable
author: zjgkkn
selftext:
Hi Reddit! A few days ago I started making my first game, and it’s already playable and is available for free download. It’s a fantasy mix of Heroes of Might and Magic 3 (the battles) and Civilization (a hex-based world map). Below are links to the game, its source code and, most importantly, the tools and workflow I use.

Download the game: [https://zjgkkn.itch.io/hexcrown](https://zjgkkn.itch.io/hexcrown)  
Source code: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/games/realms](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/games/realms)

**Assets**

All assets were made on a laptop with an RTX 3070, though more than half of the source images were generated with Codex. My current local pipeline:

1. Hunyuan3D 2.1 for the initial model.
2. Hi3D for two meshes: one with no polygon limit (usually over a million), and a low-poly one with 500 to 5,000 polygons depending on the model.
3. TRELLIS.2 paint to texture the high-poly mesh.
4. Bake the textures and normals onto the low-poly model.

Tool code: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets\_studio](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/assets_studio)

**Vector database**

I decided to make up for my lack of gamedev knowledge by loading books into a vector database: SQLite with sqlite-vec and FTS5, plus Qwen3 embeddings for semantic search. When I posted about this earlier, the comments were mixed and some developers weren’t sold on the idea, which is fair. I still kept it on by default. Without any explicit instructions from me, the model has run several hundred searches across the books, mostly on UI topics. I can’t say which decisions came from them, but the overhead is tiny, so it stays.

Tool code: [https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/games/yaqs](https://github.com/kvladsrc/gym/tree/main/games/yaqs)

**What’s next**

There’s about half an hour of gameplay right now, and I have plenty of ideas for where to take it. Mostly I want to keep building experience.

I’d really appreciate any comments and suggestions, especially on the UI and on what to build next!

comments.author: ichisay
comments.body: El repositorio de libros de desarrollo de videojuegos, quisiera saber más sobre eso y cuántos tokens puede consumir esas cientos de búsquedas para una tarea

replies.author: zjgkkn
replies.body: This is practically nothing compared to the total number of tokens. The LLM makes a query to the database consisting of a few dozen tokens and receives several fragments, each 512 tokens long. It can then, at its own discretion, load adjacent fragments to provide further context. Hundreds of such queries were made over the course of several days of nearly continuous operation meaning these few hundred queries likely account for less than 0.1% of the total.
